label: input h at original positions 0-3
explanation: Token-identity feature for the letter h, restricted to the first four original positions (t = 0..3). Fires on every h input at those positions (100% precision, ~99.9% recall) and on no other token. Magnitude depends on position: largest at t = 1 (top activations near max 1.94 are h at t = 1), strong at t = 0 and t = 2, much weaker at t = 3 (about 0.25-0.3 of max; t=3 carries ~9% of mass despite a similar count). A repeated h still fires. Does not fire on h at original positions >= 4, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (only ~50 stray copy-phase activations).

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9991, F1 0.9996, mass recall 0.99992, with 0 false positives.

The 57 test misses hold 0.0% of the activation mass. They are faint copy-phase activations (0.03-0.10 of max) on an h being copied back, mostly at step 5 for L=3, right after a strong h at t=1. This is a small, very weak echo, consistent with the 'about 50 stray copy-phase activations' the explanation already mentions.

Targeted checks confirm the claims. t=3 has 24.5% of activations but 9.3% of the mass, which works out to a mean of about 0.27 of max. t=1 holds the most mass (0.344). No activations at t=4 in the original phase, none at the delimiter, and 52 copy-phase steps in dev. A repeated h (in_first==0) still fires at precision 1.0 (3265 steps).
